scope: Authoring-prompt guidance for ordinary gameplay prose. These are guide translations, not verified official in-game aliases.
usage: Use the terms as contextual wording guidance and inflect naturally. Do not apply blanket substitutions. Preserve canonical English game, stage, character, weapon and item names, including Ride Armor. Direction variants distinguish movement from position. Examples are translation samples, not instructions for an actual stage; do not add them or their facts to guides.
review: Agent-authored terminology and examples; no native-language editorial sign-off.

terms.up-left / upper-left: hacia arriba y a la izquierda / en la parte superior izquierda
terms.up-right / upper-right: hacia arriba y a la derecha / en la parte superior derecha
terms.down-left / lower-left: hacia abajo y a la izquierda / en la parte inferior izquierda
terms.down-right / lower-right: hacia abajo y a la derecha / en la parte inferior derecha

example.source: From the ledge, dash-jump to the left wall. Climb with wall-jumps, then jump right and use an air dash to reach the platform. Stop at the ladder, look above it, and continue upward when the path is clear.
example.translation: Desde el saliente, salta con impulso hacia la pared izquierda. Sube con saltos de pared, luego salta a la derecha y usa un impulso aéreo hasta la plataforma. Detente en la escalera, mira arriba y sigue subiendo cuando el camino esté despejado.

terms.up-right / upper-right: para cima e à direita / na parte superior direita
terms.down-left / lower-left: para baixo e à esquerda / na parte inferior esquerda
terms.down-right / lower-right: para baixo e à direita / na parte inferior direita

example.translation: С уступа сделайте прыжок с рывком к левой стене. Поднимитесь прыжками от стены, затем прыгните вправо и сделайте воздушный рывок до платформы. Остановитесь у лестницы, посмотрите над ней и продолжайте вверх, когда путь будет свободен.

contexts.saber: A weapon or sword. Translate the ordinary weapon noun; never interpret it as a sage, a wise person, or the Spanish verb saber. Canonical names such as Z-Saber remain English.
contexts.supply pod: A physical container holding supplies in a stage. It is not a podcast, an abstract supply service, or a botanical seed pod.
contexts.cracked wall: A breakable wall with visible cracks. Cracks are damage in the wall, not decorative stripes. Do not add weapon requirements absent from the source.
contexts.Exit: The literal English in-game command Exit, used to leave a previously cleared stage and return to stage select. Preserve Exit as written. This context does not mean closing the pause menu and does not apply to the ordinary verb exit.
contexts.guide: This website or walkthrough document. It does not mean a person, escort, NPC, or tour guide.
contexts.enemy drops: Collectible items or loot dropped by enemies. Translate the items as the subject, not enemies falling, and never interpret drops as drones. Do not add a requirement to defeat the enemy unless stated in the source.
contexts.compound directions: The four compound entries distinguish diagonal movement from a location. Up-left means moving upward and leftward; upper-left means a position above and to the left. Up-right pairs upward with rightward, down-left pairs downward with leftward, and down-right pairs downward with rightward. Upper/lower variants describe position. Japanese naturally orders these as left-up/right-up/left-down/right-down; changing word order must never change the direction.
